title: dotnet: Make GodotSharp and generators compatible with trimming

milestone.title: 4.x
milestone.description: Issues and pull requests slated for an undetermined Godot 4 release.

body:
Depends on #116300, and #116301. This PR makes GodotSharp and the Godot source generators compatible with trimming. **What this PR DOESN'T do:** This PR doesn't implement any logic for exporting games with trimming enabled. That can come later. Editor code still relies on unreferenced code reflection and dynamic code. All such paths are annotated with `RequiresUnreferencedCode` and `RequiresDynamicCode`. Managed callbacks had to be split between the ones that are trimmer-friendly and the ones that aren't compatible with trimming. The latter are only used by the editor. Types with associated script paths now have to be registered explicitly from the entry-point (handled by source generators). By their nature, those types are rooted (always preserved), as we don't know if/when Godot will need them. I added a `[NoScriptFileAssociation]` attribute to allow manually disabling this association for a type if not desired to not root it. Types without an associated script path proved more complex. Explicit registration was a no-go because: - It gets complicated with projects where multiple assemblies declare script types (common with NuGet packages), specially if an assembly with scripts is a transitive (non-direct) dependency. - We don't want to root these types. They must only be preserved if they're used. But if they're preserved, their introspection/interop functions must also be preserved for Godot to be able to use. So basically, we required a way to tell ILLink to preserve something as long as a type is also preserved. The solution for this was in the form of attributes, since attributes are never stripped from what they annotate. For non-generic classes, the attribute implementation is simple:
Click to see ScriptTypeMetaProviderAttribute ```cs public abstract class ScriptTypeMetaProviderBaseAttribute : Attribute { public abstract ScriptTypeMeta GetGodotClassScriptMeta(Type scriptType); } [AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Class, Inherited = false)] public sealed class ScriptTypeMetaProviderAttribute< // If this attribute is preserved, also preserve the public methods T. [DynamicallyAccessedMembers(DynamicallyAccessedMemberTypes.PublicMethods)] T > : ScriptTypeMetaProviderBaseAttribute where T : IScriptTypeMetaProvider { public override ScriptTypeMeta GetGodotClassScriptMeta(Type scriptType) => return T.GetGodotClassScriptMeta(); } // Usage: // DynamicallyAccessedMemberTypes.PublicMethods will preserve 'MyScriptType.GodotInternal.MetaProvider. GetGodotClassScriptMeta()' [ScriptTypeMetaProviderAttribute(typeof(MyScriptType.GodotInternal.MetaProvider))] partial class MyScriptType : Godot.Object { protected static class GodotInternal { internal class MetaProvider : IScriptTypeMetaProvider { public static Godot.Bridge.ScriptTypeMeta GetGodotClassScriptMeta() => /* ... */; } } } ```
It gets more complex for generic types because you can't use generic type arguments in attributes. Thankfully, `DynamicallyAccessedMembers` works on strings that hold an assembly-qualified type name:
Click to see GenericScriptTypeMetaProviderAttribute ```cs [AttributeUsage(AttributeTargets.Class, Inherited = false)] public sealed class GenericScriptTypeMetaProviderAttribute : ScriptTypeMetaProviderBaseAttribute { // If this attribute is preserved, also preserve the public methods of the type with this name. [DynamicallyAccessedMembers(DynamicallyAccessedMemberTypes.PublicMethods)] private readonly string _nestedProviderGenericTypeDefinitionName; public GenericScriptTypeMetaProviderAttribute( [DynamicallyAccessedMembers(DynamicallyAccessedMemberTypes.PublicMethods)] string nestedProviderGenericTypeDefinitionName) => _nestedProviderGenericTypeDefinitionName = nestedProviderGenericTypeDefinitionName; } // Usage: // DynamicallyAccessedMemberTypes.PublicMethods will preserve 'MyScriptType<>.GodotInternal.MetaProvider. GetGodotClassScriptMeta()' [GenericScriptTypeMetaProvider("MyGenericScriptType`1+GodotInternal+MetaProvider, AssemblyName")] public class MyGenericScriptType : Godot.GodotObject { private static class GodotInternal { private class MetaProvider : IScriptTypeMetaProvider { public static Godot.Bridge.ScriptTypeMeta GetGodotClassScriptMeta() => /* ... */; } } } ```
### Backwards Compatibility Assemblies compiled against old versions of Godot use APIs that are not compatible with trimming. Additionally, some legacy APIs are rooted and waste a lot of disk space. To preserve backwards compatibility and to improve trimming, I added the MSBuild property `GodotSupportLegacyNonTrimSafeAPIs`. This property is enabled by default to avoid breaking compatibility. Projects that don't have dependencies which use those legacy Godot APIs, can set this property to `false` in their **csproj**. Disabling this property makes the project trimmable, and removes the engine->C# callbacks that those legacy dependencies rely on, effectively no longer rooting them. ### Some numbers These results are for the [Squash the Creeps (3D) C#](https://github.com/godotengine/godot-demo-projects/tree/d3337bbbe3dc2a75644eb5a0ee211f14f06e0dd5/mono/squash_the_creeps) demo project. Expect worse numbers on bigger projects. As I said, there's no exporting logic yet, but we can follow some manual steps to verify the trimming results.
The following lines were added to the demo's csproj ```csproj dotnet_SquashTheCreeps3D true true true true true false ```
Commands - **Baseline (no trimming):** `dotnet publish ./Squash\ the\ Creeps\ \(3D\).csproj -r linux-x64 --self-contained true -p:DebugType=None -p:DebugSymbols=false -p:OutputType=Exe -o ./output_baseline/` - **Trimmed:** `dotnet publish ./Squash\ the\ Creeps\ \(3D\).csproj -r linux-x64 --self-contained true -p:DebugType=None -p:DebugSymbols=false -p:PublishTrimmed=true -p:TrimMode=full -p:OutputType=Exe -o ./output_trimmed/` - **AOT:** `dotnet publish ./Squash\ the\ Creeps\ \(3D\).csproj -r linux-x64 --self-contained true -p:DebugType=None -p:DebugSymbols=false -p:PublishAot=true -o ./output_aot/` Trimming is not possible (except in AOT builds) in library projects. The Trimmed variant uses `-p:OutputType=Exe` to be able to see the results, even though it would not be usable from Godot.
Additionally, there are two sub-variants: - **Rooted**: Pass `-p:RootGodotAssemblies=true` to the command. It roots `GodotSharp` and the game assembly. This is how trimming was being done before this PR, so it can be considered a secondary baseline. - **SF**: Pass `-p:PublishSingleFile=true` to the command. It gives better results, so it's worth including.
Results | Variant | Size | |---------------------|---------| | Baseline | 80.0 MB | | Baseline SF | 72.9 MB | | Trimmed (Rooted) | 27.3 MB | | Trimmed | 21.2 MB | | Trimmed SF (Rooted) | 20.1 MB | | Trimmed SF | 14.0 MB | | AOT (Rooted) | 21.4 MB | | AOT | 4.1 MB |
The most impressive results are for AOT, for which the whole thing (project and assemblies, and .NET runtime) only take up 4.1 MB with this project (expect worse on larger projects). This can be further reduced by [disabling framework library features](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/core/deploying/trimming/trimming-options#trim-framework-library-features) that the project doesn't need.
